h: Shabbat Lights and the Restoration of the Soul
Candle lighting, challah, and niddah are connected to the refinement of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah.
Shabbat Candles and the Light of Judgment

p: בַּמִּדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא (שָׁם ב):
— In Midrash Tanchuma (there, 2):
"הַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר,
— ‘The lighting of the candle—
דִּכְתִיב: 'וְקָרָאתָ לַשַּׁבָּת עֹנֶג' – זוֹ הַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר בְּשַׁבָּת;
— for it is written: "And you shall call the Sabbath a delight"—this is the lighting of the candle on Shabbat;
וְאִם תֹּאמַר לֵישֵׁב בַּחֹשֶׁךְ, אֵין זֶה עֹנֶג,
— and if you say to sit in darkness, this is not delight,
שֶׁאֵין יוֹרְדֵי גֵיהִנָּם נִדּוֹנִין אֶלָּא בַּחֹשֶׁךְ,
— for those descending to Gehenna are judged only in darkness,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'אֶרֶץ עֵיפָתָה כְּמוֹ אֹפֶל'".
— as it is said: "A land of thick darkness, as darkness itself"’.
וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת בֹּא ב):
— And elsewhere (Midrash Tanchuma, start of Parashat Bo 2):
בַּמֶּה הָרְשָׁעִים מִתְכַּסִּים בְּגֵיהִנָּם? בַּחֹשֶׁךְ.
— With what are the wicked covered in Gehenna? In darkness.
הַגִּיגִית הַזּוֹ וְכוּלֵי,
— Like this earthenware vessel, etc.,
כָּךְ הָרְשָׁעִים: "וְהָיָה בְמַחְשָׁךְ מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם",
— so the wicked: ‘and their works are in the dark’,
לְפִיכָךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְכַסֶּה עֲלֵיהֶם שֶׁהוּא חֹשֶׁךְ,
— therefore the Holy One covers over them that which is darkness,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְחֹשֶׁךְ עַל פְּנֵי תְהוֹם" – זֶה גֵּיהִנָּם.
— as it is said: ‘and darkness was upon the face of the deep’—this is Gehenna.
וּבַגְּמָרָא (פְּסָחִים נד.) נִקְרָא "אוֹר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם";
— Yet in the Gemara (Pesachim 54a) it is called 'the light of Gehenna';
וְכֵן בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, לד עַמּוּד ב),
— and so in the holy Zohar (Part III, 34b),
דְּחָשֵׁיב שִׁבְעָה אוֹרוֹת שֶׁנִּבְרְאוּ קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם,
— where it enumerates seven lights that were created before the world was created,
חָשַׁב אוֹר גֵּיהִנָּם, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— it counts the light of Gehenna, see there.
וְהָעִנְיָן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (עֵירוּבִין יט.):
— And the matter is according to what they said in the Gemara (Eruvin 19a):
דְּפוֹשְׁעֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
— that transgressors among the idolaters,
אֲפִילּוּ עַל פִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם אֵינָם חוֹזְרִין בִּתְשׁוּבָה,
— even at the very entrance of Gehenna do not return in repentance,
וְלָהֶם הַגֵּיהִנָּם חֹשֶׁךְ,
— and for them Gehenna is darkness;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה "וְהָיָה בְמַחְשָׁךְ מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם וַיֹּאמְרוּ מִי רֹאֵנוּ וּמִי יוֹדְעֵנוּ",
— and just as in this world ‘their works are in the dark, and they say: Who sees us and who knows us?’,
כֵּן גַּם בְּגֵיהִנָּם אֵינָם חוֹזְרִין,
— so also in Gehenna they do not repent,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "הַפֹּשְׁעִים בִּי" –
— and as is stated: ‘that have transgressed against Me’—
שֶׁפּוֹשְׁעִין וְהוֹלְכִין לְעוֹלָם.
— that they continue transgressing forever.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— In contrast, regarding transgressors of Israel,
שֶׁמַּצְדִּיקִין עֲלֵיהֶם הַדִּין
— who justify the divine judgment upon themselves
וְאוֹמְרִים לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
— and say before Him: Master of the Universe,
יָפֶה דַּנְתָּ, יָפֶה זִכִּיתָ, יָפֶה חִיַּיבְתָּ וְכוּלֵי,
— well have You judged, well have You acquitted, well have You condemned, etc.,
לָהֶם נִקְרָא הַגֵּיהִנָּם "אוֹר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם";
— for them Gehenna is termed 'the light of Gehenna';
דְּכֵיוָן שֶׁנִּכְנָסִין לָהֶם – מֵאִיר לָהֶם,
— for once they enter it—it illuminates for them,
וּמַצְדִּיקִין הַדִּין עֲלֵיהֶם.
— and they acknowledge the righteousness of the judgment upon them.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְנוּ מֵחָסִיד אֶחָד
— And as we heard from a certain pious man
שֶׁאָמַר קוֹדֶם מוֹתוֹ:
— who said prior to his passing:
שֶׁמָּה לוֹ לִפְחוֹד מִגֵּיהִנָּם,
— why should he fear Gehenna,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁבּוֹ יִזְכֶּה לוֹמַר שֶׁבַח יָפֶה כָּזֶה "יָפֶה דַּנְתָּ" וְכוּלֵי.
— since therein he will merit to recite such exquisite praise: 'well have You judged, etc.'
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא "אוֹר גֵּיהִנָּם" שֶׁמֵּאִיר לָהֶם,
— Therefore it is called 'the light of Gehenna' that shines for them,
וְרַק שַׁעְתָּא חֲדָא דְּמִתְחַיְיבֵי בְּגֵיהִנָּם,
— and it is only for one hour that they are condemned in Gehenna,
וְאָתֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וּמַסֵּיק לְהוּ וּמְקַבֵּל לְהוּ.
— and Abraham our father comes, raises them up, and receives them.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 1: ‘Our teachers taught: For three transgressions women die at the time of childbirth. All three have their basis in the Torah: niddah, as it is written, ‘If a woman has a flow [of blood]’; challah, ‘The first of your dough’; and the lighting of a lamp, as it is written, ‘You shall call Shabbos a delight’—this refers to kindling the Shabbos lamp. If you should say that one might sit in darkness, that is not delight, for those who descend to Gehinnom are judged in darkness, as it says, ‘A land of deepest gloom, like darkness.’’ The Midrash continues: ‘Why were women commanded concerning these three mitzvos? ... She caused [Adam] to die and shed his blood ... She defiled the challah of the world ... She extinguished Adam’s lamp, as it is written, ‘The soul of man is the lamp of the Lord’; therefore she must attend to kindling the lamp.’

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 54a:14: “Rather, the void of Gehenna was created before the world was created, and its fire was created only on the second day of the week. And the thought arose in God’s mind to create our fire on Shabbat eve; however, it was not actually created until the conclusion of Shabbat, as it was taught in a baraita that Rabbi Yosei says: The thoughts of two phenomena arose in God’s mind on Shabbat eve, but were not actually created until the conclusion of Shabbat. At the conclusion of Shabbat, the Holy One, Blessed be He, granted Adam, the first man, creative knowledge similar to divine knowledge, and he brought two rocks and rubbed them against each other, and the first fire emerged from them. Adam also brought two animals, a female horse and a male donkey, and mated them with each other, and the resultant offspring that emerged from them was a mule. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel disagrees and says that the first mule was in the days of Anah, as it is stated: “And these are the children of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah; this is Anah who found the mules in the wilderness, as he fed the donkeys of Zibeon his father” (Genesis 36:24).”

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 54a: ‘This is no difficulty: one statement concerns our fire and one concerns the fire of Gehinnom. Our fire [was created] at the close of Shabbos; the fire of Gehinnom, on the eve of Shabbos. But was the fire of Gehinnom created on the eve of Shabbos? Was it not taught that seven things were created before the world: the Torah, repentance, the Garden of Eden, Gehinnom, the Throne of Glory, the Sanctuary, and the name of the Messiah? ... Rabbi Yose says: The fire created by the Holy One, blessed be He, on the second day never goes out, as it says, ‘Their fire shall not be quenched.’ ... Why was ‘for it was good’ not said on the second day? Because the fire of Gehinnom was created then.’

h: Shabbat as the Garden of Divine Illumination

p: וְאָמַר טַעַם זֶה לְהַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר בְּשַׁבָּת:
— And he stated this rationale for candle lighting on Shabbat:
דִּבְשַׁבָּת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרְאוּ "הַיּוֹשֶׁבֶת בַּגַּנִּים",
— for on Shabbat all Israel are called 'she that dwells in the gardens',
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ח, יג):
, — as stated (in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:13):
שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת מַשְׁכִּימִים לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת וְקוֹרִין קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וְכוּלֵי,
— that on Shabbat they arise early to the synagogue and recite the Shema, etc.,
וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אוֹמֵר לָהֶם: בָּנַי, הַגְבִּיהוּ קוֹלְכֶם וְכוּלֵי,
— and the Holy One says to them: My children, raise your voice, etc.,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּיוֹשֵׁב בְּגַן עֵדֶן,
— meaning that on Shabbat all Israel are like one dwelling in the Garden of Eden,
שֶׁהוּא שֶׁאָז מֵאִיר לָהֶם.
— which signifies that then it shines for them.
וְעֹנֶ״ג – רָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת:
— And oneg (“delight”) is an acronym for:
עֵדֶן, נָהָר, גָּן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, כו עַמּוּד א),
— Eden, Nahar (River), and Gan (Garden), as stated in the Zohar (I, 26a).
שֶׁהֵם שָׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשׁוֹת שַׁבָּת,
— which are the three sanctities of Shabbat;
וְהוּא אוֹר, הֵיפֶךְ הַגֵּיהִנָּם שֶׁהוּא חֹשֶׁךְ.
— and it is light, the absolute opposite of Gehenna which is darkness.
וְאָמַר: מָה רָאוּ נָשִׁים לְהִצְטַוּוֹת עַל שָׁלֹשׁ מִצְווֹת הָאֵלּוּ וְכוּלֵי?
— And he said: Why were women commanded concerning these three mitzvos, etc.?
שָׁפְכָה אֶת דָּמוֹ וְכוּלֵי – תִּשְׁפּוֹךְ דָּמָהּ וְתִשְׁמוֹר נִדָּתָהּ וְכוּלֵי;
— She spilled his blood, etc.—let her shed her blood and observe her niddah, etc.;
חַלָּה – הִיא טִמְּאָה חַלָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי;
— challah—she defiled the challah of the world, etc.;
הַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר – הִיא כִּבְּתָה נֵרוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם וְכוּלֵי;
— candle lighting—she extinguished the candle of man, etc.;
וּבַגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת לב.):
— and in the Gemara (Shabbat 32a):
"נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַתִּי בָּכֶם קְרוּיָה נֵר,
— “The soul that I placed within you is called a lamp;
עַל עִסְקֵי נֵר הִזְהַרְתִּי אֶתְכֶם", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— concerning the lamp I warned you,” see there.
וּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים אֵלּוּ כְּנֶגֶד פְּגַם אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
— And these three things correspond to the blemish of Adam the First
שֶׁהָיָה בְּנֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ וּנְשָׁמָה,
— which manifested in nefesh, ruach, and neshamah,
וְהָיָה עַל יְדֵי גְּרַם חַוָּה.
— and was brought about through Chavah.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: הִיא טִמְּאָה חַלָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם – כְּנֶגֶד הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
— This is what he meant by “she defiled the challah of the world”: it corresponds to the nefesh,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: כָּךְ עָשָׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
— and as they said: so the Holy One did with Adam the First,
דִּכְתִיב: "וְאֵד יַעֲלֶה מִן הָאָרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּיצֶר ה' אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם עָפָר וְגוֹמֵר",
— for it is written: ‘and a mist rose from the earth... and Hashem God formed man of the dust, etc.’,
וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
— and it corresponds to the nefesh,
דִּכְתִיב: "תּוֹצֵא הָאָרֶץ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה",
— for it is written: ‘Let the earth bring forth living nefesh’,
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, יב עַמּוּד א):
— and it is taught in the holy Zohar (Part II, 12a):
"דָּא נַפְשָׁא דְּאָדָם קַדְמָאָה".
— ‘this is the nefesh of primordial man’.
וְאַף דְּשָׁם הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר מִבַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים,
— And even though Scripture there speaks of animals,
נִכְלָל בּוֹ גַּם נֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם שֶׁהוּא חַיּוּת הַגּוּף.
— there is subsumed within it also the nefesh of man which is the vitality of the physical body.
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתַב "הִיא שָׁפְכָה אֶת דָּמוֹ" הוּא כְּנֶגֶד הָרוּחַ שֶׁהוּא בַּלֵּב.
— And the statement “she shed his blood” corresponds to ruach, which resides in the heart.
וּבַגְּמָרָא הַלָּשׁוֹן: "רְבִיעִית דָּם נָתַתִּי בָּכֶם",
— And the Gemara uses the expression: “A quarter-log of blood I placed within you,”
וְהַיְינוּ רְבִיעִית דָּם שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
— meaning the revi'it of blood in the heart,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת (סוֹטָה ה.):
— and as Tosafot wrote (Sotah 5a):
רְבִיעִית דָּם הוּא דָּם הַצָּלוּל שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ מַשְׁתִּית הַלֵּב וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— a revi'it of blood is the pure blood from which the heart's foundation is formed, etc., see there.
וְאַף דִּכְתִיב: "כִּי הַדָּם הוּא הַנָּפֶשׁ",
— And even though it is written: ‘for the blood is the nefesh’,
הַיְינוּ דָּם שֶׁבַּכָּבֵד וְדַם כָּל הָאֵבָרִים;
— that refers to the blood in the liver and the blood of all limbs;
וּרְבִיעִית דָּם הַיְינוּ הַצָּלוּל שֶׁבַּלֵּב
— whereas the revi'it of blood is the clear blood in the heart,
וְשָׁם מִשְׁכַּן הָרוּחַ,
— and there is the dwelling place of the ruach,
וּכְנֶגֶד זֶה אָמַר: "תִּשְׁמוֹר נִדָּתָהּ",
— and corresponding to this it said: ‘let her observe her niddah’,
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְכַּפֵּר לָהּ עַל דַּם הָאָדָם שֶׁשָּׁפְכָה.
— so that it atone for her for the blood of man that she spilled.
וְהַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר כְּנֶגֶד פְּגַם הַנְּשָׁמָה,
— And candle lighting corresponds to the blemish of the neshamah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא: נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַתִּי בָּכֶם קְרוּיָה נֵר וְכוּלֵי,
— and as they said in the Gemara: the soul I placed in you is called a candle, etc.,
וּכְתִיב: "נֵר ה' נִשְׁמַת אָדָם".
— and it is written: ‘The spirit of man is the lamp of Hashem’.

h: Three Mitzvot and Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah

p: וְנִתְּנוּ הַשָּׁלֹשׁ מִצְווֹת לְתַקֵּן הַפְּגָם שֶׁבְּנֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ וּנְשָׁמָה.
— And the three mitzvot were given to rectify the blemish in nefesh, ruach, and neshamah.
וְלָכֵן מִצְוַת חַלָּה וְנִדָּה נוֹהֵג בְּכָל יוֹם,
— Therefore the mitzvot of challah and niddah apply every day,
הַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר רַק בְּשַׁבָּת,
— while candle lighting is uniquely on Shabbat,
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (סב עַמּוּד א):
— based on what is written in the holy Zohar in this parashah (62a):
נֶפֶשׁ וְרוּחַ כְּלִילָן דָּא עִם דָּא וְכוּלֵי,
— nefesh and ruach are intertwined with one another, etc.;
אָתָא בַּר נָשׁ לְאִתְדַּכָּאָה –
— when a man comes to purify himself—
מְסַיְּיעִין לֵיהּ בְּנִשְׁמְתָא קַדִּישָׁא וְכוּלֵי
— they assist him with a holy neshamah, etc.,
וּמְקַדְּשִׁין לֵיהּ וְאִקְרֵי קָדוֹשׁ.
— and sanctify him, and he is called holy.
וּבְכָל יוֹם יֵשׁ לָאָדָם נֶפֶשׁ וְרוּחַ;
— And on every weekday a person possesses nefesh and ruach;
וּבְשַׁבָּת, דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, פח עַמּוּד ב):
— whereas on Shabbat, as is taught in the holy Zohar (Part II, 88b):
בְּשַׁבַּתָּא יָהֲבִין לֵיהּ לְבַר נָשׁ נִשְׁמְתָא אַחֲרָא וְכוּלֵי,
— on Shabbat they grant man an additional soul, etc.,
נִשְׁמְתָא דְּכָל שְׁלֵימוּ בָּהּ כְּדוּגְמָא דְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי,
— a soul wherein is all perfection like the archetype of the World to Come,
שֶׁזּוֹכֶה כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל לִנְשָׁמָה.
— for every single Jew merits this neshamah.
וְכֵן בַּגְּמָרָא (בֵּיצָה טז.),
— And so in the Gemara (Beitzah 16a),
אַף שֶׁלָּמְדוּ מִדִּכְתִיב: "וַיִּנָּפַשׁ" – וַי, אָבְדָה נֶפֶשׁ,
— even though they derived it from the verse 'and He rested' (vayinafash)—woe, the soul is lost,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ הַלָּשׁוֹן:
— nonetheless they used the terminology:
"נְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה נוֹתֵן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּאָדָם וְכוּלֵי",
— ‘An additional neshamah the Holy One, blessed be He, places in man, etc.’;
וְזֶהוּ "וּמְקַדְּשִׁין לֵיהּ וְאִקְרֵי קָדוֹשׁ",
— and this is ‘they sanctify him and he is called holy’,
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לָדַעַת כִּי אֲנִי ה' מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם".
— in the manner of that which is stated: ‘to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you’.
וְעַל כֵּן מִצְוַת חַלָּה וְנִדָּה
— Therefore, the mitzvot of challah and niddah,
שֶׁבָּאוּ לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְהָרוּחַ,
— which came to rectify the blemish of the nefesh and the ruach,
מִצְוָתָן כָּל הַיָּמִים;
— their obligation applies on all days;
וּמִצְוַת הַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר בְּשַׁבָּת
— while the mitzvah of candle lighting is on Shabbat,
לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם מֵהַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִפְּגַם הַנָּחָשׁ.
— to rectify the blemish of the neshamah stemming from the Serpent's fall.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "וּבִמְנַרְתָּא טָבְתָא דְּנָהֲרָא עַל רֵישִׁין",
— And as we recite in the Sabbath hymns: ‘and with a good menorah shining upon our heads’,
וְהַיְינוּ הַנְּשָׁמָה,
— which refers to the neshamah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁזּוֹכִין בִּמְעֵי אִמּוֹ:
— just as one merits in his mother's womb:
"וְנֵר דָּלוּק לוֹ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ,
— ‘and a candle is lit above his head,
וְצוֹפֶה וּמַבִּיט בּוֹ מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ,
— and he gazes and sees by it from one end of the world to the other,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'בְּהִלּוֹ נֵרוֹ עֲלֵי רֹאשִׁי'"
— as it is said: "When His lamp shined upon my head"’
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב נִדָּה ל:);
— (as written in Niddah 30b);
וְהַיְינוּ "נֵר ה' נִשְׁמַת אָדָם",
— and this is ‘The spirit of man is the lamp of Hashem’,
דְּנִקְרָא "נֵר ה'" לְהָאִיר לוֹ אוֹר זֶה
— for it is termed 'the lamp of Hashem' to radiate unto him this illumination
דְּהַכָּרַת כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מִכָּל הַבְּרִיאָה,
— of recognizing the glory of His sovereignty from all Creation,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁזֶּהוּ הָאוֹר שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּיוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן
— and as we said, this is the light created on the first day
שֶׁהָיָה הָאָדָם צוֹפֶה וּמַבִּיט בּוֹ מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ,
— whereby man gazed and saw from one end of the universe to the other,
דְּהַיְינוּ לְהַכִּיר מִכָּל הַבְּרִיאָה כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— namely to perceive from all of Creation the glory of His sovereignty.
וּבִמְעֵי אִמּוֹ הַנֵּר עַל רֹאשׁוֹ,
— And in his mother's womb the lamp is above his head,
כִּי בְּעוֹדוֹ בִּמְעֵי אִמּוֹ עֲדַיִן אֵין בּוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע,
— for while still in his mother's womb he does not yet possess an evil inclination,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (סַנְהֶדְרִין צא:) מִקְּרָא דְּ"לַפֶּתַח חַטָּאת רֹבֵץ";
— as stated (Sanhedrin 91b) from the verse ‘sin couches at the door’;

p: וּכְמוֹ כֵן בְּשַׁבָּת הַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה,
— And likewise on Shabbat the additional neshamah,
דְּאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ דְּכָל שְׁלֵימוּ בָּהּ כְּדוּגְמָא דְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי,
— concerning which they said in the holy Zohar that all perfection is within it like the World to Come,
הוּא גַּם כֵּן הַנֵּר שֶׁעַל הָרֹאשׁ,
— is also the lamp above the head,
שֶׁהוּא אוֹר מַקִּיף
— which is an encompassing light (Ohr Makif)
שֶׁאֵין שְׁלִיטָה לְיֵצֶר הָרָע בְּשַׁבָּת.
— such that the evil inclination has no dominion on Shabbat.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא):
— Therefore they said (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 11):
בֵּרְכוֹ בַּמְּאוֹרוֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם,
— ‘He blessed it with luminaries’, see there,
דְּמַשְׁמָע שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת יֵשׁ הִתְגַּלּוּת מֵאוֹתוֹ אוֹר דְּיוֹם א'.
— which indicates that on Shabbat there is a revelation of that light of the first day.
וּמְפוֹרָשׁ גַּם בְּסֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר (אוֹת קס):
— And it is explicit also in Sefer HaBahir (section 160):
לָקַח שְׁבִיעִי וְשָׂם לָהֶם בִּמְקוֹמוֹ,
— He took the seventh and set it for them in its place,
וְהַשְּׁאָר גְּנָזוֹ לַצַּדִּיקִים.
— and the rest He concealed for the righteous.
וְעַל יְדֵי נֵר שַׁבָּת מְתַקְּנִים פְּגַם הַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁל אָדָם
— And through the Sabbath candle we rectify the blemish of man's neshamah
וְנִיצּוֹלִים מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
— and are saved from the evil inclination,
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "וּבִמְנַרְתָּא טָבְתָא דְּנָהֲרָא עַל רֵישִׁין".
— and this is what is meant by ‘and with a good menorah shining upon our heads’.
וּבְחוֹל, שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִי שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה וְאִית בֵּיהּ תְּרֵין דַּרְגִּין נֶפֶשׁ וְרוּחַ,
— And on weekdays, where there is one who has not merited and possesses only two levels, nefesh and ruach,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
— as written in the holy Zohar,
בָּא מִצְוַת חַלָּה וְנִדָּה
— the mitzvot of challah and niddah come
לְתַקֵּן הַפְּגָם שֶׁל הַנָּחָשׁ בִּשְׁתֵּי מַדְרֵיגוֹת נֶפֶשׁ וְרוּחַ, וְכָאָמוּר.
— to rectify the blemish of the Serpent in the two levels of nefesh and ruach, as explained.
וּבָא פְּתִיחָה זוֹ בְּרֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ
— And this opening discourse appears at the beginning of Parashat Noach
עַל פִּי מַה שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ מֵהַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וּמֵהַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה,
— based on what we explained from the holy Zohar and Midrash Rabbah,
שֶׁבְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל הָיָה נֶפֶשׁ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
— that in the Generation of the Flood the soul of Moses our teacher was present
וְהָיָה הַזְּמַן לִיתֵּן לָהֶם הַתּוֹרָה,
— and it was the time to give them the Torah,
וְיֵשׁ לָזֶה רֶמֶז גַּם בַּגְּמָרָא (כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְמַעְלָה);
— and there is an allusion to this in the Gemara as well (as explained above);
וּמִסְּתָמָא הָיָה אָז הַזְּמַן לְתַקֵּן כָּל פְּגַם הַנָּחָשׁ
— and presumably it was then the time to rectify the entire blemish of the Serpent
בְּכָל הַשָּׁלֹשׁ מַדְרֵיגוֹת נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ וּנְשָׁמָה.
— across all three levels: nefesh, ruach, and neshamah.
וְאַחַר שֶׁקִּלְקְלוּ
— And after they corrupted their ways
וְנֶהֶפַךְ לְמַיִם הַזֵּידוֹנִים וּמֵי הַמַּבּוּל –
— and the waters turned into raging waters and the waters of the Flood—
"עַל שָׁלֹשׁ עֲבֵירוֹת אֵלּוּ נָשִׁים מֵתוֹת וְכוּלֵי".
— ‘for these three transgressions women die, etc.’
וּבְשַׁבָּת הַזְּמַן לְתַקֵּן כָּל הַפְּגָם,
— And on Shabbat is the time to rectify the entire blemish,
וְאַלְמָלֵי מְשַׁמְּרִין כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל הַשַּׁבָּת כְּהִלְכָתָן – מִיָּד נִגְאָלִין מִכֹּל וָכֹל,
— and had all Israel kept the Sabbath according to its halakhot—they would immediately be redeemed entirely,
שֶׁהָיָה נַעֲשָׂה הַתִּיקּוּן לְגַמְרֵי;
— for the rectification would be completely accomplished;
רַק הָעוֹלָם נִידּוֹן אַחַר רוּבּוֹ.
— only that the world is judged according to its majority.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, כָּל נֶפֶשׁ בִּפְרָט הַמְשַׁמֵּר שַׁבָּת כְּהִלְכָתוֹ – מִיָּד נִגְאָל:
— Nonetheless, every individual soul who observes Shabbat according to its halakhah—is immediately redeemed.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 11:2: ““God blessed the seventh day [and sanctified it]” – Rabbi Yishmael said: He blessed it with manna and He sanctified it with manna. He blessed it with manna in that all the days of the week one omer [of manna] would fall, while on the day before Shabbat two omers would fall. He sanctified it with manna, as it did not fall on it [on Shabbat] at all. Rabbi Natan says: He blessed it with manna and sanctified it with a blessing. Rabbi Yitzḥak said: He blessed it with manna and sanctified it through the gatherer. He blessed it with apparel. Rav Huna said: He should change his clothing. Rabbi Ḥiyya said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: He should mix [garments]. Avin bar Ḥisdai said: He should lower [his garments]. Rabbi Yirmeya and Rabbi Ze’eira were walking together [on Shabbat], and the outer garment of Rabbi Yirmeya was raised up, but Rabbi Ze’eira lowered his. This shows that one should lower [one’s garments for Shabbat]. Rabbi Elazar says: He blessed it with [the Shabbat] candle, and there was an incident involving me [that illustrates this]. One time I kindled a candle on Shabbat eve, and I came and found it burning at the conclusion of Shabbat, and nothing [of the oil] was diminished. He blessed it with the radiance of a person’s face, He sanctified it with the radiance of a person’s face. The radiance of a person’s face all the days of the week is not comparable to the way it is on Shabbat. He blessed it with the lights. Rabbi Shimon bar Yehuda of Kefar Akko says in the name of Rabbi Shimon: Even though the lights were cursed on the day before Shabbat, they were not stricken until the conclusion of Shabbat. This is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, and not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ami, as Rabbi Ami said: Adam the first man, his glory did not spend the night with him. What is the source? “Man [adam] will not go to rest in his splendor; he is like the beasts that perish” (Psalms 49:13). The Rabbis say: His glory did spend the night with him, and only at the conclusion of Shabbat was his radiance taken from him, as He expelled him from the Garden of Eden. That is what is written: “You alter his countenance and send him away” (Job 14:20). When the sun set on Shabbat eve, the Holy One blessed be He sought to put away the [primordial] light, but He accorded honor to Shabbat. That is what is written: “God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it” – He blessed it with light. When the sun set on Shabbat eve the [primordial] light continued to function. Everyone began praising [God]; that is what is written: “Under all the heavens they sing His praises, and His light is to the ends of the earth” (Job 37:3). Why was this? Because “His light is to the ends of the earth.” Rabbi Yehuda bar Rabbi Simon said: By the light that the Holy One blessed be He created on the first day, a person could look out and see from one end of the world to the other end. When the Holy One blessed be He looked at the people of the generation of the Flood and the people of the generation of the Dispersion, whose actions were to be corrupt, He arose and hid it away and designated it for the righteous in the future. From where is it derived that He hid it away? It is as it is stated: “Their light will be withheld from the wicked, and the upraised arm will be broken” (Job 38:15). And from where is it derived that He designated it for the righteous in the future? It is as it is stated: “But the path of the righteous is like a dawning light, growing brighter until the day is established” (Proverbs 4:18). Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Ze’eira: That [primordial] light functioned for thirty-six hours – twelve on the day before Shabbat, twelve on the night of Shabbat, and twelve on Shabbat. As the sun set at the conclusion of Shabbat, darkness began approaching, and Adam the first man became afraid, as it is stated: “And I said that darkness will envelop me [yeshufeni]; night for me is light,” (Psalms 139:11) – that one [the serpent] in whose regard it is written: “He will strike your head [yeshufekha], and you will strike his heel [teshufenu]” (Genesis 3:15), is now coming to confront me. What did the Holy One blessed be He do? He prepared for him two flint stones and he struck them one against the other. Light emerged from them and he recited a blessing over it. That is what is written: “Night for me is light.” What blessing did he recite over it? [Blessed be God] Who creates the lights of fire. This is in accordance with the opinion of Shmuel, as Shmuel said: Why does one recite a blessing over light at the conclusion of Shabbat? It is because that time was the beginning of its creation. Rav Huna in the name of Rav and Rabbi Abahu in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One recites a blessing over it [light] at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, as well, because fire rested all that day.”

paragraphs.text: Sefer HaBahir 160: “This teaches that before the world was created, it arose in thought to create a great light to illuminate. A great light was created which no creature could master. The Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw that they could not bear it. He took a seventh and placed it there for them, and stored away the rest for the righteous in the future. He said: “If they merit this seventh and guard it, I will give them this in the final world.” This is the World to Come, which had already come before the six days of Creation.”

paragraphs.text: Pri Tzaddik, Sefer Kedushas Shabbos 7:26: “This is “The soul of man is Hashem's lamp” (Mishlei 20:27): it is a portion of the light hidden away for the righteous, through which they gaze from one end of the world to the other, as mentioned above. As stated in Pesachim 8a, the righteous in the presence of the Divine Presence are like a lamp before a torch. Concerning the torchlight of His Divine Presence, it is said, “Man shall not see Me and live” (Shemos 33:20); only at the moment of death by a divine kiss does the lamp cleave and join to the torch. The soul can comprehend then, but not while clothed in the physical body. Before a person has emerged into the world, however, the soul is not yet fully clothed so as to enter the body's interior; rather, it stands as a surrounding light over his head.
